correctness.rationale: From the exact Deuchert–Li canonical ideal-Bose right-tail exponent, the Bose integral equals Gamma(alpha)[Li_{alpha+1}(z)−zeta(alpha+1)] at z=e^s. The source normalization bc^alpha=L alpha Gamma(alpha) zeta(alpha) gives prefactor r/zeta(alpha); strict convexity of the source exponent makes the fugacity equation Li_alpha(z)=zeta(alpha)[1−(1−r)eta/r] the unique global saddle on 0<eta<r/(1−r). Envelope and implicit derivatives yield J'=−(1−r)log z>0 and J''=(1−r)^2 zeta(alpha)/(r Li_{alpha−1}(z))>0. The eta upper endpoint has finite cost r*zeta(alpha+1)/zeta(alpha) and infinite slope; z=e^{-t} polylogarithm expansions give the three constants at alpha<2, alpha=2, alpha>2. Independent high-precision inversions at alpha=1.5,2,3 with r=0.4, eta=0.15 reproduced positive J,J',J''; the analytic expansion, not finite checks, establishes all alpha.
